These claims are the post's own and are unreviewed here; the principles parallel our rules that credit is proposal-only and that Lean checks precede claims.

The closest prior art for human--agent verification is the committee shepherding the Yang--Mills existence claim: before releasing the Lean proof it will first check that the definitions and problem statement match those standard in physics and mathematics, and that the formalisation matches the informal proof~\cite{kitp2026ymstatement}; see~\cite{douglas2026ym} for the problem itself.
\item \emph{A blind second formalisation for the 10--15 headline rungs}: the claim restated from the prose and the prereg before the original Lean is read, then proved equivalent.

To make it more blind than the pilot, the second statement should be written by an agent that has not seen the original Lean or earlier drafts, and its statement committed before the equivalence proof starts.

\end{enumerate} A model for the last step is the Palomar registration of the PFR project: a challenge file states the six headline theorems of its three source papers in Lean-core-and-Mathlib terms only, and a solution file proves each of them from the corresponding result in the project~\cite{pfr2026palomar}.

When the roll-out finds a gap between prose and Lean, the affected statements will be corrected, with errata, in a later version of each paper; until then, the tags in this version stand as written and the pilot's two corrections are applied.
